transcribed_from: Step 6.7a S2.2f (2026-10-12): structure of the upper floor for light wood platform framing. Client decisions 2026-10-12 12:31: joist span 20 ft (I-joists), interior structural axes as a hard rule, upper-floor cantilever 3 ft, family room upstairs allowed as a loft at the arrival. Code references (CRC R602.10 wall bracing, R301.2.2.6 irregular buildings in seismic design category D) are transcribed from secondary sources and stay unverified. Version 0.2.0 (S2.2g, client 2026-10-12 18:45): structural frame first (support and infill, SAR) with positions by optimization; central hall with two axes for upper floors 30-40 ft deep; ground surplus to a porch or a smaller footprint; the stair core is one more axis candidate; multi-plane roofs.
verification_note: Design values, not an engineering design: the generator keeps walls stacked and spans within the limits so that a prescriptive (non-engineered) light-frame design stays possible; every value verified=false until an engineer checks it.

parameter_schema.note: Every value the client or the designer may define is a parameter object: value, type (number / enum / list / bool), unit, kind (hard / soft / weight / reference), who (client / designer / code), range (numbers), choices (enum / list), kinds_allowed, optional floor (a code rule the value may not cross) and a description in Spanish and English. The design registry (modules/design) reads them; the client's changes go to a design profile, never here.

text: Walls of the upper floor are perimeter, structural (zone walls: on an axis shared with a ground-floor wall) or partitions (inside a zone, on the floor joists).
A wall run stands on the ground-floor walls of the same line; the unsupported pieces are beams between supports (ground walls on the line or crossing it), each at most beam_span_max_ft.
Ground spaces under the upper floor span at most joist_span_max_ft on their short side; an open boundary of the great room under the upper floor is a beam.

line_wall_bonus.note: A frame line inside a zone needs a wall or a beam in stage S2.1; a line that is a zone wall has it by construction.

text: The joists span the upper floor's short side S; the axes run along its long side.
S <= joist span: no interior axis; up to spine_from_ft: one axis; up to twice the joist span: a central hall with two axes. The upper outline lines and the joint over the ground floor are axes too.
Both floors band on the same axes; the upper bands are the bays; the ground band cut lies on an axis and the other axes are walls or beams on the axis.

Positions (optimize): a free axis moves within its window to the position with the least area deviation plus the surplus cost; then the zone walls of both floors move (within the snap reach) to align across floors, each aligned wall worth align_bonus_sqft of area deviation (a small MILP on HiGHS); every result is checked again exactly.

source.document: S2.2g research (2026-10-12): Habraken/SAR support and infill; Merrell et al. 2010; MIQP/MILP layout (Wu et al. 2018)
